states.name: Alabama
states.summary: Tax lien auctions (counties that opted in) or tax certificate sales, 3-year redemption.
states.conducted_by: County Revenue Commissioner / Tax Collector
states.sale_timing: Spring (most counties April through June)
states.bidding: Tax lien auctions: interest bid down from 12%. Certificate sales: premium bid.
states.redemption: 3 years from the sale
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgage foreclosures are trustee/attorney sales on the courthouse steps. The Sheriff sells property only on court judgments (executions).
states.notes: Since 2019 counties may hold tax lien auctions instead of tax sales; most larger counties now do, online through GovEase.

states.name: Alaska
states.summary: Boroughs foreclose in court and sell the land; no property tax (and no sales) in the unorganized borough.
states.conducted_by: Borough or municipal finance/land office (after court foreclosure)
states.sale_timing: Periodic land sales set by each borough
states.bidding: Sealed bid or outcry, borough by borough
states.rate: Interest and penalties set by borough ordinance
states.redemption: 1 year after the foreclosure judgment, before the borough takes the deed; none after the borough sells
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are foreclosed nonjudicially by the trustee. Court-ordered sales are rare.
states.notes: Only organized boroughs and cities levy property tax (Anchorage, Fairbanks North Star, Mat-Su, Kenai, Juneau and others). Census areas in the unorganized borough have no tax sales.

states.name: Arizona
states.summary: Tax lien certificates sold every February; interest bid down from 16%; 3 years before foreclosure.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: February
states.bidding: Interest rate bid down from 16%
states.redemption: 3 years, then the lien holder may foreclose in court
states.sheriff_sales: Most mortgages are deeds of trust sold by the trustee. Judicial foreclosures and executions are sold by the County Sheriff.
states.notes: Liens not sold at auction are struck to the state and can be bought over the counter from the Treasurer.

states.name: Arkansas
states.summary: The state Commissioner of State Lands auctions tax-delinquent parcels county by county.
states.conducted_by: Commissioner of State Lands (state agency)
states.sale_timing: Year-round, each county scheduled once a year; unsold parcels move to post-auction sale
states.bidding: Premium bid, live and online
states.redemption: Owners may redeem until the sale; a short post-sale waiting period applies before the deed issues
states.sheriff_sales: Most mortgages are foreclosed nonjudicially (Statutory Foreclosure Act) by the trustee; judicial foreclosures end in Commissioner's sales.
states.notes: Counties certify delinquent parcels to the state after about two years; the Commissioner of State Lands handles the sale and the deed.

states.name: California
states.summary: Tax Collectors sell tax-defaulted property outright, usually online, after 5 years of default.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer-Tax Collector
states.sale_timing: Most sales February through May; some counties sell twice a year
states.bidding: Premium bid (deposit required), almost all online
states.redemption: Ends at 5 p.m. the day before the sale; none afterwards (1-year window to challenge the sale)
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgages are mostly deeds of trust sold by the trustee. The Sheriff sells on judicial foreclosures and money judgments.
states.statute: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 3691 et seq.
states.notes: Excess proceeds go to former owners and lienholders who claim within a year. Properties can be sold after 3 years when a nuisance abatement lien exists.

states.name: Colorado
states.summary: Tax lien sales each fall; premium bids earn no interest; 3 years before a treasurer's deed.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: October through the second Monday of December
states.bidding: Premium bid (the overbid is not returned and earns no interest)
states.rate: Federal discount rate plus 9 points, set each September (about 13% to 15% in recent years)
states.redemption: 3 years from the sale, then the holder may apply for a treasurer's deed
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are foreclosed through the county Public Trustee, who holds the sale. The Sheriff sells on judicial foreclosures and HOA liens.
platforms: RealAuction and Zeus Auction (most counties online)
states.notes: Colorado is unusual in that premium bids are a pure cost to the buyer, so liens tend to sell close to face value.

states.name: Connecticut
states.summary: Towns sell the property at a tax sale; the owner has 6 months to redeem at 18% interest.
states.conducted_by: Municipal Tax Collector (cities and towns; Connecticut has no county government)
states.sale_timing: Set by each town as needed
states.bidding: Premium bid
states.rate: 18% per year on the amount paid
states.redemption: 6 months after the sale
states.sheriff_sales: All foreclosures are judicial. Court-ordered 'foreclosure by sale' auctions are run by a court-appointed committee, not the sheriff; strict foreclosure (no sale) is also common.
states.notes: The Census now uses nine planning regions as county equivalents; the tax sales themselves happen at the town level, so each region tab lists the towns inside it.

states.name: Delaware
states.summary: Sheriffs sell tax-delinquent parcels at monthly monition sales; owners get 60 days after confirmation to redeem.
states.conducted_by: County Sheriff (monition sale after a court writ)
states.sale_timing: Monthly sheriff sales (New Castle, Kent and Sussex each set their day)
states.bidding: Premium bid at the sheriff sale
states.rate: Penalty of 15% to 20% of the bid, depending on the county
states.redemption: 60 days after the court confirms the sale
states.sheriff_sales: Delaware is a judicial foreclosure state; the County Sheriff holds mortgage foreclosure and tax (monition) sales, typically monthly.
platforms: Sheriff sale listings on each county site
states.notes: Only three counties. New Castle County moved its sheriff sales online.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.summary: Annual tax lien sale each July; 18% interest; 6 months before a foreclosure suit can be filed.
states.conducted_by: Office of Tax and Revenue
states.sale_timing: July
states.bidding: Premium bid (premium is not returned if the lien is redeemed within the first months of the holding period)
states.redemption: 6 months, after which the holder may file to foreclose the right of redemption
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are foreclosed by the trustee after notice to the Mayor; there is no sheriff sale venue.
states.notes: Owner-occupied homes with small balances are excluded from the sale.

states.name: Florida
states.summary: Tax certificates every June (interest bid down from 18%), then tax deed auctions by the Clerk once a certificate is 2 years old.
states.conducted_by: Tax Collector (certificates); Clerk of Court (tax deed auctions)
states.sale_timing: Certificate sale by June 1; tax deed auctions year-round, usually monthly
states.bidding: Certificates: interest bid down from 18% (5% minimum return). Tax deeds: premium bid, mostly online.
states.rate: Up to 18% per year on certificates (5% mandatory minimum)
states.redemption: Owner can redeem until the tax deed is sold; no redemption after the deed sale
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgage foreclosures are judicial; the Clerk of Court (not the sheriff) holds the sale, in most counties online. Sheriff sales are limited to executions on judgments.
states.notes: Clerk foreclosure sales and tax deed sales run on the same online platforms, so one county portal usually lists both.

states.name: Georgia
states.summary: Tax deeds sold on the courthouse steps the first Tuesday of the month; 12-month redemption with a 20% penalty.
states.conducted_by: Tax Commissioner (ex officio sheriff) or Sheriff; some counties use judicial in rem sales
states.sale_timing: First Tuesday of the month, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at the courthouse
states.bidding: Premium bid, cash or certified funds the same day
states.rate: 20% penalty in the first year, 10% for each year after, plus 20% after the barment notice
states.redemption: 12 months after the sale (until the right is barred by notice)
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgage foreclosures are nonjudicial, also on the first Tuesday on the courthouse steps, run by the lender's attorney. The Sheriff levies and sells on judgments.
states.notes: Excess funds from the sale belong to the former owner and lienholders and are a large part of the Metro Atlanta tracker.

states.name: Hawaii
states.summary: Counties sell tax-delinquent property at public auction; owner may redeem within a year at 12%.
states.conducted_by: County Director of Finance / Real Property Tax Division
states.sale_timing: As needed (sales are infrequent)
states.bidding: Premium bid
states.redemption: 1 year after the sale
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgage foreclosures are judicial, sold by a court-appointed commissioner. Sheriff sales are for executions.
states.statute: HRS § 246-55 et seq. and county codes
states.notes: Four counties levy property tax (Honolulu, Maui, Hawaii, Kauai); Kalawao is administered by the state Department of Health.

states.name: Idaho
states.summary: The county takes a tax deed after 3 years and the Board of Commissioners auctions it.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer (tax deed) and Board of County Commissioners (auction)
states.sale_timing: As needed after tax deed, often once a year
states.bidding: Premium bid at public auction
states.redemption: Owner may redeem until the county sells the property
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee. The Sheriff sells on judicial foreclosures and executions.
platforms: County Commissioners' sales, some online (Idaho Auction, Bid4Assets)
states.notes: Excess proceeds are paid to the former owner since a 2016 law change.

states.name: Illinois
states.summary: Annual tax sale of liens with the penalty rate bid down; 6 months to 2.5 years to redeem depending on the property.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer (sale) and County Clerk (redemptions); Cook County holds a separate scavenger sale
states.sale_timing: Each county sets its own date, mostly in the fall and winter after the second installment
states.bidding: Penalty rate bid down from 9% per six months (cut from 18% for sales from 2024 on)
states.redemption: 2 years for most property, 2.5 years for owner-occupied homes of 1 to 6 units, 6 months for vacant and commercial parcels
states.sheriff_sales: Illinois is judicial; the County Sheriff (or a court-appointed selling officer such as Judicial Sales Corp in Cook County) holds the foreclosure sale.
platforms: Joseph E. Meyer & Associates (iltaxsale.com, most downstate counties)
states.notes: Cook County's Scavenger Sale offers liens with 3 or more years of unpaid taxes with no minimum bid.

states.name: Indiana
states.summary: Fall tax sale of lien certificates (1-year redemption), then a Commissioners' certificate sale with a 120-day redemption.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer and Auditor (Treasurer's sale); Board of Commissioners (certificate sale)
states.sale_timing: Treasurer's sale August through October; Commissioners' sales winter and spring
states.bidding: Premium bid
states.rate: 10% of the minimum bid if redeemed within 6 months, 15% after; 5% per year on the overbid
states.redemption: 1 year (120 days for Commissioners' certificates)
states.sheriff_sales: Indiana is judicial; the County Sheriff holds mortgage foreclosure sales, many of them online.
states.notes: SRI also runs many Indiana sheriff sales, so one portal covers both.

states.name: Iowa
states.summary: Tax sale the third Monday of June; 2% per month; bidders bid down the share of the parcel they would take.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: Third Monday in June
states.bidding: Bid down the undivided percentage interest; ties by random draw
states.redemption: 1 year 9 months, then the holder serves a 90-day notice of expiration
states.sheriff_sales: Iowa is judicial; the County Sheriff holds foreclosure sales (many through iowasheriffsales.com).
platforms: Iowa Tax Auction (iowataxauction.com) and county sites
states.notes: Adjourned sales continue monthly for parcels not sold in June.

states.name: Kansas
states.summary: Counties foreclose in court after 3 years and the Sheriff sells the property; no redemption after the sale.
states.conducted_by: County Counselor / Treasurer files suit; County Sheriff holds the sale
states.sale_timing: As needed after judgment, usually once or twice a year
states.bidding: Premium bid at the sheriff sale
states.redemption: Until the sale; none afterwards
states.sheriff_sales: Kansas is judicial; the County Sheriff sells mortgage foreclosures and tax foreclosures, often with an online option.
platforms: Some counties on civicsource.com or purplewave.com
states.notes: Sales are confirmed by the court; the former owner may not bid.

states.name: Kentucky
states.summary: County Clerks sell certificates of delinquency after the Sheriff's collection ends; 12% interest; foreclosure after 1 year.
states.conducted_by: County Clerk (certificate sale); Sheriff collects earlier in the year
states.sale_timing: July through October, on a date set by the Clerk
states.bidding: Lottery or priority order; certificates sell at face value
states.redemption: Owner may redeem at any time; the holder may file to foreclose after 1 year
states.sheriff_sales: Kentucky is judicial; the court's Master Commissioner, not the sheriff, holds foreclosure sales.
platforms: County Clerk sites and the Department of Revenue's third-party purchaser registry
states.notes: Third-party purchasers must register with the Department of Revenue.

states.name: Louisiana
states.summary: Parish tax sales historically sold a redeemable interest (3-year redemption, 5% penalty plus 1% a month); a 2024 constitutional amendment moves the state to tax lien auctions from 2026.
states.conducted_by: Parish Tax Collector (the Sheriff in most parishes; the City of New Orleans in Orleans)
states.sale_timing: Once a year per parish, many in late spring and early summer
states.bidding: Historically bid down the ownership percentage; lien auctions under the new system bid down interest
states.rate: 5% penalty plus 1% per month under the old system
states.redemption: 3 years (18 months for blighted or abandoned property)
states.sheriff_sales: Louisiana is judicial (executory process); the Parish Sheriff holds mortgage foreclosure sales, many online through CivicSource.
states.statute: La. R.S. 47:2151 et seq.; La. Const. art. VII § 25 as amended in 2024
states.notes: Confirm the current procedure with the parish: the change to tax lien auctions was approved by voters in December 2024 and takes effect for 2026 sales.

states.name: Maine
states.summary: Municipalities file tax liens that foreclose automatically after 18 months; the town then sells the property.
states.conducted_by: Municipal Tax Collector and the town (counties play no role)
states.sale_timing: Town sales as needed
states.bidding: Sealed bid or auction set by the town
states.rate: Interest at the municipal rate (about 8% to 9%)
states.redemption: 18 months after the lien is recorded, then the lien forecloses automatically
states.sheriff_sales: Maine is judicial; after judgment the lender holds a public sale (not a sheriff sale).
states.notes: A 2023 law requires towns to sell foreclosed homes and return the surplus to the former owner.

states.name: Maryland
states.summary: Annual tax lien sales in May and June; interest set by county (6% to 20%); foreclosure after 6 months.
states.conducted_by: County Finance Office / Treasurer; Baltimore City Department of Finance
states.sale_timing: May and June (Baltimore City in May)
states.bidding: Premium bid (high bid premium rules vary by county)
states.rate: 6% to 20% per year depending on the county
states.redemption: 6 months before a foreclosure suit can be filed (9 months for owner-occupied homes in Baltimore City)
states.sheriff_sales: Foreclosures are 'quasi-judicial': the trustee sells after filing in court. The Sheriff sells only on executions.
states.notes: Owner-occupied homes below a balance threshold are withheld in several counties.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.summary: Cities and towns take tax title (16% interest) and foreclose through the Land Court; some assign liens to investors.
states.conducted_by: Municipal Treasurer / Collector
states.sale_timing: Tax takings and lien assignments as scheduled by each municipality
states.bidding: Tax title assignments by sealed bid or auction
states.redemption: Until the Land Court enters a foreclosure decree (at least 1 year after the taking)
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgages are foreclosed by power of sale at an auction run by the lender's auctioneer. No sheriff sale venue.
platforms: Tallage and other lien buyers' listings
states.notes: A 2024 reform (after Tyler v. Hennepin) returns surplus equity to former owners.

states.name: Michigan
states.summary: County Treasurers foreclose after 3 years and auction the property, mostly online in late summer and fall.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer (foreclosing governmental unit)
states.sale_timing: July through November, two rounds (minimum bid, then no minimum)
states.bidding: Premium bid, online
states.rate: Not applicable (deed sale); 1% per month plus fees before foreclosure
states.redemption: Until March 31 of the foreclosure year; none after the judgment
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgages are foreclosed by advertisement with a weekly Sheriff's sale at the courthouse, followed by a 6-month redemption period.
states.notes: Former owners can claim remaining proceeds under a 2020 law that followed Rafaeli v. Oakland County.

states.name: Minnesota
states.summary: Property forfeits to the state after the redemption period; the county then sells tax-forfeited land.
states.conducted_by: County Auditor / Land Department
states.sale_timing: Public auctions set by each county, often spring and fall
states.bidding: Premium bid at public auction; unsold parcels then sell over the counter
states.redemption: 3 years from the judgment (5 years for homesteads and some other classes) before forfeiture; none after
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgages are foreclosed by advertisement with a Sheriff's sale, followed by a 6-month (sometimes 12-month) redemption period.
platforms: County auditor and land department sites
states.notes: Minnesota's forfeiture process was the subject of Tyler v. Hennepin; surplus is now returned to former owners.

states.name: Mississippi
states.summary: Tax lien sale the last Monday of August; 1.5% per month; 2-year redemption through the Chancery Clerk.
states.conducted_by: County Tax Collector (sale); Chancery Clerk (redemptions and deeds)
states.sale_timing: Last Monday in August (some counties also the first Monday in April)
states.bidding: Premium bid (the overbid earns no interest)
states.redemption: 2 years from the sale
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee on the courthouse steps. The Sheriff sells on executions.
states.notes: Parcels not sold are struck off to the state and sold by the Secretary of State's Public Lands division.

states.name: Missouri
states.summary: County Collectors hold tax sales the fourth Monday of August; 1-year redemption at 10% for first and second offerings, shorter for later ones.
states.conducted_by: County Collector of Revenue; St. Louis City and Jackson County use court-ordered Sheriff sales
states.sale_timing: Fourth Monday in August
states.bidding: Premium bid
states.rate: 10% per year on the purchase price, 8% on subsequent taxes paid
states.redemption: 1 year (first and second offerings), 90 days (third offering), none for later offerings
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee. St. Louis City and Jackson County tax foreclosures (Land Tax Suits) are sold by the Sheriff.
platforms: Jackson County and St. Louis City sheriff sale pages
states.notes: Buyers must be Missouri residents or appoint a resident agent and must certify they owe no delinquent taxes.

states.name: Montana
states.summary: Tax liens attach each summer; investors buy assignments from the county; 3 years to redeem at 10% plus a 2% penalty.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: Liens attach in July; assignments are sold afterwards, often first-come
states.bidding: Assignment at face value (first-come or lottery, by county)
states.redemption: 3 years from the lien date
states.sheriff_sales: Trust indentures are sold by the trustee. The Sheriff sells on judicial foreclosures and executions.
states.notes: Since 2017 the county, not investors, is the initial lien holder; investors take assignments.

states.name: Nebraska
states.summary: Tax lien certificates sold the first Monday in March at 14%; 3-year redemption.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: First Monday in March
states.bidding: Round-robin or bid down of the undivided interest, by county
states.redemption: 3 years from the sale
states.sheriff_sales: Nebraska is judicial for mortgages; the County Sheriff holds foreclosure sales. Trust deeds may be sold by the trustee.
states.notes: After 3 years the holder can apply for a treasurer's deed or foreclose in court.

states.name: Nevada
states.summary: The County Treasurer holds property in trust after 3 years and sells it at a trustee auction; no redemption after the sale.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer (as trustee)
states.sale_timing: Set by each county (Clark County usually May; Washoe usually April)
states.bidding: Premium bid; Clark County requires a registration deposit
states.redemption: Until the sale; none afterwards (the IRS keeps a 120-day right on federally liened parcels)
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee. The Sheriff sells on judicial foreclosures and executions.
states.notes: The Clark County tracker in this project reads the Treasurer's auction endpoints directly.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.summary: Towns execute tax liens (14% interest) and take a tax collector's deed after 2 years if unredeemed.
states.conducted_by: Municipal Tax Collector (towns and cities)
states.sale_timing: Liens executed each spring; town sales of deeded property as needed
states.bidding: Most towns keep the lien themselves and later sell the property at auction
states.redemption: 2 years from the lien before the collector's deed
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgages are foreclosed by power of sale at a public auction run by the lender. No sheriff sale venue.
states.notes: A 2023 law requires surplus from town sales to be returned to the former owner.

states.name: New Jersey
states.summary: Municipalities hold annual tax lien sales; interest bid down from 18% then premiums; foreclosure after 2 years.
states.conducted_by: Municipal Tax Collector (565 municipalities; counties play no role)
states.sale_timing: Each municipality once a year, many online
states.bidding: Interest bid down from 18% to 0%, then premium bids
states.rate: Up to 18% per year plus 2% to 6% penalties
states.redemption: 2 years before the holder may foreclose (6 months for the municipality)
states.sheriff_sales: New Jersey is judicial; the County Sheriff holds mortgage foreclosure sales, most of them weekly and many online.
states.notes: A 2024 law lets owners force a judicial sale to protect their equity when a lien is foreclosed.

states.name: New Mexico
states.summary: The state Property Tax Division auctions delinquent property county by county after 3 years; no redemption after the sale.
states.conducted_by: Taxation and Revenue Department, Property Tax Division (state agency)
states.sale_timing: Year-round, each county scheduled in turn
states.bidding: Premium bid, live and online
states.redemption: Until the sale; none afterwards (a limited 2-year window exists to challenge the sale)
states.sheriff_sales: New Mexico is judicial; a court-appointed Special Master holds foreclosure sales.
states.notes: Counties send the delinquent list to the state, which runs the whole sale.

states.name: New York
states.summary: Most counties foreclose in rem after 2 years and auction deeds; NYC, Nassau and Suffolk sell tax liens instead.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer / Commissioner of Finance (upstate); NYC Department of Finance (lien sale)
states.sale_timing: County auctions mostly spring through fall; NYC lien sale usually May
states.bidding: Premium bid, mostly online through auction houses
states.rate: NYC liens 9% to 18%; Nassau and Suffolk liens bid down from 10% to 12%
states.redemption: 2 years from the lien date before the county forecloses; none after the judgment
states.sheriff_sales: New York is judicial; a court-appointed Referee, not the sheriff, holds foreclosure sales.
states.notes: A 2024 state law requires counties to return surplus to former owners.

states.name: North Carolina
states.summary: Counties foreclose in court; sales close only after a 10-day upset-bid period; no redemption after confirmation.
states.conducted_by: County Tax Collector through a foreclosure attorney; sale by a court-appointed commissioner
states.sale_timing: Continuous, as foreclosures reach judgment
states.bidding: Auction at the courthouse, then upset bids (at least 5% or $750 more) for 10 days each
states.redemption: Owner may pay in full until the sale is confirmed; none afterwards
states.sheriff_sales: Deed-of-trust foreclosures go through a Clerk of Court hearing and a trustee sale with the same upset-bid process. The Sheriff sells on executions.
platforms: County tax office and foreclosure attorney sites (Zacchaeus Legal, Kania Law, etc.)
states.notes: Some counties use the faster in rem (§ 105-375) method sold by the Sheriff.

states.name: North Dakota
states.summary: The county takes a tax deed after 3 years and sells the parcels at an annual sale the third Tuesday in November.
states.conducted_by: County Auditor
states.sale_timing: Third Tuesday in November
states.bidding: Premium bid, minimum of taxes and costs
states.redemption: Until October 1 of the year the county takes the deed; the former owner may repurchase before the sale
states.sheriff_sales: North Dakota is judicial; the County Sheriff holds foreclosure sales.
states.notes: Unsold parcels can be bought from the county afterwards.

states.name: Ohio
states.summary: Larger counties sell tax lien certificates; every county also forecloses in court with Sheriff sales (two offerings).
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer (liens) and Prosecutor; County Sheriff holds foreclosure sales
states.sale_timing: Lien sales once or twice a year in larger counties; sheriff sales weekly or monthly
states.bidding: Liens: negotiated bulk sales or interest bid down from 18%. Sheriff sales: premium bid, two-thirds of appraisal at the first offering
states.rate: Up to 18% per year on lien certificates
states.redemption: Lien holders may foreclose after 1 year; owners may redeem until the court confirms a sheriff sale
states.sheriff_sales: Ohio is judicial; the County Sheriff holds mortgage and tax foreclosure sales, online statewide since 2022 (sheriffsaleauction.ohio.gov).
platforms: County treasurer and land bank sites
states.notes: County land banks and Boards of Revision handle abandoned parcels through expedited foreclosure. Forfeited land sales follow unsold second offerings.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.summary: County Treasurers hold the June Resale (second Monday of June) for parcels 3 years delinquent; no redemption after.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: Second Monday in June
states.bidding: Premium bid, minimum of two-thirds of assessed value or taxes due
states.redemption: Until the sale; none afterwards
states.sheriff_sales: Oklahoma is judicial for most mortgages; the County Sheriff holds foreclosure sales.
states.notes: Unsold parcels are deeded to the county and sold through commissioners' sales.

states.name: Oregon
states.summary: Counties foreclose after 3 years; owners get 2 more years to redeem; the county then sells surplus property.
states.conducted_by: County Tax Collector (foreclosure) and County Commissioners / Property Management (sales)
states.sale_timing: County surplus property sales as scheduled
states.bidding: Public auction or sealed bid by county
states.rate: Not applicable (deed sale); 16% during the redemption period
states.redemption: 2 years after the foreclosure judgment
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee. The Sheriff sells on judicial foreclosures and executions.
platforms: Some counties on Bid4Assets or GovDeals
states.notes: Oregon counties keep the land until the redemption period ends, so sales lag delinquency by about 5 years.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.summary: Tax Claim Bureaus hold the Upset Sale in September, then Judicial and Repository sales; Philadelphia and Allegheny use Sheriff sales.
states.conducted_by: County Tax Claim Bureau (65 counties); Sheriff under the Municipal Claims Act in Philadelphia and Allegheny
states.sale_timing: Upset Sale in September; Judicial Sales in winter and spring; Repository year-round
states.bidding: Premium bid; Upset Sale parcels carry existing liens, Judicial Sale parcels are free and clear
states.redemption: None after Tax Claim Bureau sales; 9 months for owner-occupied property after Philadelphia and Allegheny sheriff tax sales
states.sheriff_sales: Pennsylvania is judicial; the County Sheriff holds monthly mortgage foreclosure sales, many online through Bid4Assets.
states.statute: 72 P.S. § 5860 (Real Estate Tax Sale Law); 53 P.S. § 7101 (MCTLA)
platforms: Bid4Assets (Philadelphia sheriff sales and many Tax Claim Bureaus)
states.notes: Bidders must pre-register at least 10 days before a sale under a 2021 law.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.summary: Cities and towns sell tax titles; owners have 1 year to redeem with a 10% penalty plus 1% a month after 6 months.
states.conducted_by: Municipal Tax Collector
states.sale_timing: Each municipality as needed
states.bidding: Bid down the undivided interest
states.rate: 10% penalty, plus 1% per month after the sixth month
states.redemption: 1 year, then the buyer may petition the Superior Court to foreclose
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgages are foreclosed by power of sale at a public auction run by the lender. No sheriff sale venue.
states.notes: Rhode Island's five counties have no government; the tracker lists the municipalities in each.

states.name: South Carolina
states.summary: Tax sales in the fall; the owner has 1 year to redeem, paying 3% a quarter up to 12% (capped at the opening bid).
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer / Delinquent Tax Collector
states.sale_timing: October through December (many on the first Monday in December)
states.bidding: Premium bid
states.rate: 3% per quarter up to 12%, capped at the amount of the opening bid
states.redemption: 1 year from the sale
states.sheriff_sales: South Carolina is judicial; the Master-in-Equity (or Special Referee), not the sheriff, holds foreclosure sales, usually the first Monday of the month.
states.notes: Mobile homes are sold at the same sales.

states.name: South Dakota
states.summary: Tax certificates sold the third Monday of December at 10%; 3 years to redeem (4 for homesteads). Many counties now keep the certificates.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: Third Monday in December
states.bidding: Face value, by lot where competitive
states.redemption: 3 years (4 years for owner-occupied homesteads)
states.sheriff_sales: South Dakota is judicial; the County Sheriff holds foreclosure sales.
states.notes: Counties that opted out of public certificate sales take the tax deed themselves and sell the land.

states.name: Tennessee
states.summary: Chancery Court tax sales run by the Clerk and Master; 1-year redemption (shorter for vacant and abandoned parcels) at 12%.
states.conducted_by: County Trustee refers to the Delinquent Tax Attorney; Clerk and Master holds the sale
states.sale_timing: Set by each county's Chancery Court, often several times a year
states.bidding: Premium bid, live or online
states.rate: 12% per year on the purchase price
states.redemption: 1 year, which the court may shorten to 30 to 180 days for vacant, abandoned or long-delinquent parcels
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee on the courthouse steps. The Sheriff sells on executions.
states.notes: Shelby County (Memphis) and Davidson County (Nashville) hold large recurring sales.

states.name: Texas
states.summary: Sheriff or Constable sales the first Tuesday of the month; 2-year redemption for homesteads and farmland (25%/50% penalty), 180 days for the rest.
states.conducted_by: County Sheriff or Constable after a court judgment; delinquent tax law firms (Linebarger, Perdue Brandon, MVBA) manage the suits
states.sale_timing: First Tuesday of the month, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at the courthouse or designated venue
states.bidding: Premium bid; many counties require a written statement that the bidder owes no delinquent taxes
states.rate: 25% penalty in the first year, 50% in the second (homestead and agricultural); 25% for other property
states.redemption: 2 years for homesteads, agricultural land and mineral interests; 180 days for everything else
states.sheriff_sales: Deed-of-trust foreclosures are trustee sales held the same first Tuesday at the same venue. The Sheriff and Constables hold tax sales, resales of struck-off parcels and execution sales.
platforms: In person at each county's venue
Online in some counties (RealAuction for Tarrant and others; mvbataxsales.com; pbfcm.com)
states.notes: Resale lists (property struck off to the taxing units) are posted by the law firms and sold with no minimum in many counties.

states.name: Utah
states.summary: County Auditors hold the May Tax Sale for parcels delinquent 4 years (sold in the 5th); no redemption after the sale.
states.conducted_by: County Auditor (with the Treasurer and Commission)
states.sale_timing: May (many counties the fourth Thursday); some counties sell in June
states.bidding: Premium bid or 'preferred' bid down of the undivided interest, by county
states.redemption: Until the sale; none afterwards
states.sheriff_sales: Trust deeds are sold by the trustee. The Sheriff sells on judicial foreclosures and executions.
states.notes: Salt Lake and Utah counties publish the list about a month before the sale.

states.name: Vermont
states.summary: Town delinquent tax collectors sell the property; the owner has 1 year to redeem at 12%.
states.conducted_by: Municipal Delinquent Tax Collector
states.sale_timing: Each town as needed
states.bidding: Premium bid
states.redemption: 1 year from the sale
states.sheriff_sales: Vermont is judicial; sales are ordered by the court and run by the plaintiff or a court-appointed officer.
states.notes: Counties have no role in Vermont tax sales.

states.name: Virginia
states.summary: Treasurers sue in Circuit Court; a Special Commissioner auctions the parcel, often online; no redemption after the sale.
states.conducted_by: County or City Treasurer through a tax sale attorney (TACS, Sands Anderson, etc.); sale by a Special Commissioner
states.sale_timing: Year-round as cases reach judgment
states.bidding: Premium bid, live or online, subject to court confirmation
states.redemption: Owner may pay in full until the sale (or confirmation); none afterwards
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee. The Sheriff sells on executions.
states.notes: Virginia's 38 independent cities run their own sales alongside the 95 counties.

states.name: Washington
states.summary: County Treasurers foreclose after 3 years and auction the property, mostly online, in late fall.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: November and December in most counties
states.bidding: Premium bid, online in the larger counties
states.redemption: Until the day before the sale; none afterwards (minors and incapacitated owners excepted)
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee. The Sheriff sells on judicial foreclosures with an 8- or 12-month redemption period.
states.notes: Surplus from the sale is held for the former owner for 3 years.

states.name: West Virginia
states.summary: Since 2022 delinquent liens go to the State Auditor, who auctions them; 12% interest and a redemption period before the deed.
states.conducted_by: State Auditor's Office (Land Division); County Sheriffs collect and certify
states.sale_timing: Auditor's auctions scheduled county by county, mostly online
states.bidding: Premium bid
states.redemption: Until the Auditor issues the deed after the statutory notice period (confirm the current timeline with the Auditor)
states.sheriff_sales: Deeds of trust are sold by the trustee. The Sheriff no longer holds the annual tax sale.
states.statute: W. Va. Code § 11A-3 (as amended by SB 552, 2022)
states.notes: The 2022 law ended county sheriff tax lien sales and centralized them with the State Auditor.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.summary: Counties hold the tax certificates (12%), take a tax deed after 2 years, and sell the land, often online.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer (certificates and deed); County Board / Treasurer sells the land; Milwaukee City handles its own
states.sale_timing: County land sales as scheduled, many online
states.bidding: Sealed bid or online auction by county
states.rate: 1% per month (12% per year) while the county holds the certificate
states.redemption: 2 years from the certificate date before the county takes the deed; none after
states.sheriff_sales: Wisconsin is judicial; the County Sheriff holds weekly mortgage foreclosure sales (many online through RealAuction or the county).
states.notes: Wisconsin does not sell certificates to the public; the county is the lien holder.

states.name: Wyoming
states.summary: Tax lien certificates sold each September at 15% plus a 3% penalty; 4-year redemption.
states.conducted_by: County Treasurer
states.sale_timing: September (dates set by each treasurer)
states.bidding: Random draw or rotation, by county
states.redemption: 4 years from the sale
states.sheriff_sales: Mortgages are foreclosed by advertisement with a Sheriff's sale, followed by a 3-month redemption period.
states.notes: Buyers who hold a certificate through the fourth year apply to the treasurer for a deed.

states.name: Puerto Rico
states.summary: Property tax is collected by CRIM; delinquent-property auctions (subastas) are infrequent and run centrally.
states.conducted_by: CRIM (Centro de Recaudación de Ingresos Municipales)
states.sale_timing: As announced by CRIM
states.bidding: Public auction
states.redemption: Per CRIM procedure
states.sheriff_sales: Foreclosures are judicial through the Court of First Instance; the court marshal (alguacil) holds the sale.
states.statute: Ley 83-1991 (Ley de Contribución Municipal sobre la Propiedad)
states.notes: Included because the Census lists its 78 municipios as county equivalents.
